prompt:
A wide illustration for the pre-fight screen of a mythology card game, showing an enemy in its own scene, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain clearly showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour. A limited palette of 4 or 5 colours, dark overall. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting, no glow, no soft gradients, no depth of field, no fine detail or texture rendering, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art. Composition: the enemy described below stands in the middle of the scene, full length and large, painted into it with exactly the same outlines, washes, paper grain and palette as everything around it and lit by the scene's own light, so figure and setting are one picture; the setting continues all around it. The bottom strip of the picture stays a little darker and calmer for a name to be written over it. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no logo, no signature.

Setting: Yellow Wind Ridge from Journey to the West, where the Yellow Wind Demon blows his sand-storm: wind-carved ochre cliffs and sandstone pillars along the left and right edges; a howling yellow sand-wind swirling in great curling bands across the top; the demon's cave fortress with a tattered banner at the far left; a lone pilgrim's dropped bamboo hat and staff half-buried in sand at the lower right; scrub pines bent flat by the wind The brush rhythm of Chinese ink-wash painting mixed into the pen-and-ink style. Distinctly Chinese: no Japanese, Greek or Norse elements.
Colour: near-black umber to golden ochre (#241d07 to #c9a227) with amber, rust red and a little jade-green accent.

In the scene: The Yellow Wind Demon, a sable-weasel demon king in yellow armour with a trident, a swirl of yellow sand around his hands. Chinese, Ming dynasty, Journey to the West. A calm, confident, casual pose, at ease: the body turned three-quarters, the head turned to look straight at the viewer. Not attacking, not shouting.
